chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi from Ja'far ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman from al-Husayn ibn Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said:

Qudamah ibn Mazyun was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab after he had drunk wine, and two men testified against him. One testified that he saw him drinking, and the other testified that he saw him vomiting wine. Umar sent for some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), among them was the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and said to him: 'What do you say, O Abu al-Hasan? For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to you: You are the most knowledgeable of this nation and the most just in ruling with the truth.' And these two have differed in their testimony. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'He who vomits it has drunk it.' He asked: 'Does the testimony of the eunuch (or one with little beard) suffice?' He said: 'The loss of his beard is like the loss of some of his limbs.'

key_terms.أَقْضَاهَا بِالْحَقِّ: The most just in ruling with the truth

ai.seo_question: What was Imam Ali's ruling on the testimony of wine drinkers when witnesses differed on whether they saw them drinking or vomiting?
ai.summary: In this juristic precedent from the era of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) demonstrates the principle of 'qarīnah' (circumstantial evidence) by ruling that vomiting confirms prior consumption, thereby resolving the discrepancy between the two witnesses. The narration further elucidates the legal capacity of individuals with physical anomalies, such as eunuchs or those with sparse beards, affirming their eligibility for testimony based on the integrity of their remaining faculties. This incident highlights the early application of nuanced evidentiary standards within the broader Islamic legal tradition, emphasizing practical reasoning over rigid formalism.
